vulnerabilities.description: Key validation uses basic regex. While adequate for intended purpose, consider adding length limits to prevent DOS via extremely long keys.
Session context values should validate types to prevent unexpected JSON serialization issues.
Uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML with hardcoded content (safe), but pattern could be misused if logic changes. Monitor for future modifications.
Expression parser uses toLowerCase() on input. Safe from injection, but consider documenting expected case-sensitivity behavior.

hardcodedSecrets.details: No API keys, passwords, or secrets found. All sensitive config uses environment variables.

sqlInjection.details: No SQL injection risks - this is a static site generator with no database queries.

xssVulnerabilities.details: XSS properly mitigated. React auto-escapes by default. Only one dangerouslySetInnerHTML use with hardcoded content.

insecureDependencies.details: All dependencies current and maintained. Next.js 14.2.35, React 18, no known vulnerabilities.

authenticationAuthorization.details: Public read-only application. No sensitive authentication vectors exposed.

inputValidation.details: Calculator inputs properly validated. Uses safe expression parser instead of eval().

filePathTraversal.details: All file operations use controlled paths. No user input in file paths.

commandInjection.details: Uses spawnSync() with array arguments, avoiding shell interpretation.

recommendations: Run 'npm audit' regularly to catch dependency updates
Add Content-Security-Policy headers in production deployment
Monitor Next.js security advisories and update regularly
Add size limits for localStorage values if they grow
Validate edge cases in calculator inputs (very large numbers, scientific notation)
passedSecurityChecks: ✓ Static site generation reduces attack surface
